title: Cocktail 2 Drops Its Trailer on May 29. The Original Made ₹122 Crore and Every NRI Wedding Playlist. This Sequel Has a Plagiarism Scandal and Shahid Kapoor.
excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna replace the original trio for a June 19 release. Pritam returns as composer, but his first single already faces Italian copyright claims. The bar is absurdly high.
body:
If you grew up in the Indian diaspora in the 2010s, there's a very good chance you heard 'Angreji Beat' at a wedding, a Diwali party, a college cultural night, and at least fourteen house parties in between. Cocktail didn't just make ₹122 crore at the box office in 2012. It became the background score of a generation of NRIs who were figuring out what it meant to be Indian abroad.

Now, fourteen years later, Cocktail 2 is coming. The trailer drops May 29. The film releases June 19. And the conversation has already started — not about the film itself, but about whether a sequel can capture what the original didn't even try to.

## The New Cast, the Same Director

Homi Adajania returns to direct. That's the good news. The original Cocktail worked because Adajania understood that a film about three people falling in love in London was really a film about the three versions of Indian identity that coexist in every NRI's head — the traditional one (Diana Penty's Meera), the liberated one (Deepika Padukone's Veronica), and the one stuck in between (Saif Ali Khan's Gautam).

The new cast is Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna. Produced by Dinesh Vijan's Maddock Films and Luv Ranjan, with filming completed across Sicily and Delhi. Dimple Kapadia and Sanjay Dutt join the supporting cast. Varun Dhawan has a cameo. The infrastructure is expensive.

But Shahid Kapoor is not Saif Ali Khan. Saif's Gautam worked because Saif carried the effortless privilege of a man who'd never had to try too hard at anything — a quality that made his eventual emotional vulnerability devastating. Shahid, for all his considerable skill, projects intensity. He tries hard. That's a different energy for a Cocktail film.

## The Pritam Problem

Pritam's original Cocktail soundtrack is, by any measure, one of the greatest Bollywood pop albums of the last fifteen years. 'Tumhi Ho Bandhu' is a friendship anthem that still closes NRI house parties at 2 AM. 'Daaru Desi' became a cultural shorthand. 'Angreji Beat' crossed over into mainstream awareness in a way few Hindi film songs manage.

Pritam returns for the sequel. The first single, 'Mashooqa,' has already generated controversy. Listeners almost immediately identified its melodic similarity to a 1993 Italian track, 'Se So Arrubate A Nonna.' Pritam has pushed back against the plagiarism claims, calling them "unfair" and "unrealistic." The second single, 'Tujhko,' featuring Arijit Singh, has been better received — a soft summer ballad that Sacnilk described as emphasizing "emotional intimacy over grand gestures."

The issue isn't whether Pritam copied an Italian song. The issue is whether the Cocktail 2 soundtrack can exist in the same emotional universe as the original. The 2012 album didn't just accompany the film — it outlived it. Cocktail's songs are still in rotation on NRI playlists twelve years later. That's the bar.

## What the Box Office Says About the Opportunity

Cocktail 2 releases into a June 2026 market that Bollywood desperately needs to win. May was dominated by regional cinema — Suriya's Karuppu (₹253 crore worldwide), Drishyam 3 (₹170 crore), and the surprise Marathi hit Raja Shivaji (₹114 crore). Bollywood's May entries — Pati Patni Aur Woh Do (₹54 crore) and Chand Mera Dil (₹21 crore) — underperformed badly.

The romantic comedy genre, specifically, hasn't produced a major hit since Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar in 2023 (₹223 crore). Industry trackers peg Cocktail 2's opening potential at double digits, with a worldwide ceiling of ₹150 crore if word-of-mouth holds. To crack the all-time top 10 rom-com list, it would need to beat Pati Patni Aur Woh's ₹109 crore — achievable, but not guaranteed.

## The Diaspora Calculation

Here is the thing about Cocktail's legacy in the diaspora: it was never really about the film. It was about recognition. For NRIs in London — and by extension, NRIs everywhere — the original Cocktail was one of the first mainstream Bollywood films that depicted their world without exoticizing it. The London in that film wasn't a tourist brochure. It was flat shares and nightclubs and the particular kind of confusion that comes from living between two cultures.

Whether Cocktail 2 can replicate that depends on something no trailer can answer: does it understand that the diaspora has changed? The NRI of 2012 was still figuring out social media. The NRI of 2026 has built businesses, started families, watched their parents age over FaceTime, and developed a much more complicated relationship with "going back."

Sicily is a beautiful filming location. But the emotional geography of the sequel needs to be more than European vistas and designer outfits. It needs to acknowledge that the people who loved the original have grown up — and that growing up, for an NRI, is its own kind of cocktail.

*Cocktail 2 trailer drops May 29, 2026. Theatrical release June 19, 2026.*
